It was obtained and finished in **1989**.

Oil platform in the Gulf of Mexico

Platform being towed out to sea

**Bullwinkle** is a 1,736 feet (529 m)[[1]]#cite_note-1) tall, pile-supported fixed steel [oil platform] in the [Gulf of Mexico]. Installed in 1988, the total weight of the platform is 77,000 tons, of which the steel jacket comprises 49,375 tons.[[2]]#cite_note-2) At the time of its construction it was the third tallest freestanding structure ever built–shorter than only the [CN Tower] and the [Ostankino Tower]–and the tallest in the United States, being 6 ft (1.8 m) taller than the pinnacle of the [Sears Tower]. Of the total height, 1,352 feet (412 m) are below the [waterline]. It is located in [Green Canyon Block 65]"), approximately 160 miles (260 km) southwest of [New Orleans]. Bullwinkle currently is operated by Talos Energy, LLC. The total field development construction cost was US$500,000,000 according to some sources.[[3]]#cite_note-3)[[4]]#cite_note-4)

The jacket, i.e. the mainly submerged part of the platform, was built by [Gulf Marine Fabricators]") in 1985–1988 at the North Yard location in [Ingleside, Texas], at the intersection of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel and the Intracoastal Waterway in [Port Aransas], east of [Corpus Christi].[[5]]#cite_note-5) The platform was shipped using a barge and installed by [Heerema Marine Contractors].[[6]]#cite_note-6) The jacket, which is some 1,400 feet tall, is the second tallest object ever to be moved to another position (relative to the surface of the Earth), after the [Troll A platform].

The Bullwinkle platform is the third tallest freestanding structure built in water after the [Petronius] and [Baldpate] "Baldpate (oil platform)")[Compliant Towers], but it is the tallest of these that could be built on land as is without any modifications.

In 2010, [Superior Energy Services] took ownership of the platform and planned to decommission it at the end of its economic life.[[7]]#cite_note-7)[[8]]#cite_note-8)
